description: Archie Studio default capability — native filesystem (the TauriFsBridge surface) + folder dialog, scoped to the app-data dir and the user's home. Opener globs (Archie-2139) cover github.com (device login, commit, settings/pages), *.github.io (the published site), docs.github.com (the custom-domain guide) — never https://**. DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH ONLY: the opener plugin matches with glob's default options, where * crosses /, so the *.github.io entry cannot pin the hostname; the load-bearing check is the hostname allowlist in publish-machine's openExternal (isAllowedExternalUrl).

permissions.comment: Archie-be3a (decided 2026-07-27): `http://**` REMOVED — cleartext is not granted. Every caller of the native-http bridge (apps/studio/src/tauri-fs.ts fetchRemoteAsBlobUrl / fetchRemoteJson) is a remote IIIF image, an info.json, or remote AV, and all of them are https in practice. NOTE the failure mode is clean, which is why this is safe to tighten: the plugin refuses, tauriFetch throws, and the caller falls back to the webview path — whose CSP allows `https:` only on img-src/media-src/connect-src, so a cleartext URL surfaces the ordinary 'couldn't load this media item' rather than hanging. If a plain-http institutional IIIF host ever has to be supported, the escape hatch is a NARROW per-host entry here, never restoring the wildcard. Tauri's internal http://asset.localhost and http://ipc.localhost are unaffected: they are webview protocols, not this plugin's scope.

Archie-7b48: the `.*` entries are LOAD-BEARING, not defensive. Tauri matches scope globs with a leading-dot rule, so a `**` wildcard does NOT match a path component that starts with a dot — and Archie writes two of them: `.bake-schema` (asset-store.ts, one per assets dir) and `.archie-cache/` (resident-store.ts, the desktop-only hidden peaks cache). Without these, fs.exists('.bake-schema') is refused as `forbidden path`, the asset save job REJECTS AFTER the bytes have already landed, and the ingest misreports it as 'couldn't store on this device — free some space' on a disk with a terabyte free. Measured 2026-07-26 on a packaged build. Note $APPDATA/** alone covers library.json because $APPDATA expands to a LITERAL path (the dots in .local are not matched by a wildcard); only the trailing dot-components need these extra entries.
